s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent perianal abscesses with atypical squamous cells and a fluctuant mass
key_facts: 66-year-old man
History of perianal trauma from sitting on broken glass in childhood
Comorbidities include vascular dementia, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, atrial fibrillation, and gout
No perianal warts, sexually transmitted diseases, immune deficiency, inflammatory dermatoses, arsenic exposure, or family history of malignancy
Fluctuant left lateral perianal mass without external fistulas
Ultrasound‐guided aspiration yielded 15 cc of purulent fluid
Gram stain and cultures were negative
Cytology showed atypical squamous cells
Mass enlarged over two months
Surgical drainage yielded purulent fluid without microbial growth
External sinus tract into the mass noted on examination under anesthesia

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma

raw.rationale: Cytology showed atypical squamous cells, which is a strong indicator of malignancy, particularly in the context of a recurrent and enlarging perianal mass

rejected.label: Anorectal abscess
rejected.why: While the patient had recurrent abscesses, the presence of atypical squamous cells and the mass's enlargement despite drainage suggest a more complex underlying condition

rejected.label: Hidradenitis suppurativa
rejected.why: There is no mention of inflammatory dermatoses or other characteristic features of hidradenitis suppurativa

rejected.label: Perianal cyst
rejected.why: The presence of atypical squamous cells and the mass's behavior are not typical of a simple cyst

rejected.label: Fistula-in-ano
rejected.why: No fistula to the anal canal was noted on examination under anesthesia, making this diagnosis less likely
